account:
It is late morning on day 0, and I am at the bakery stall during my scheduled market walk. Nothing I have observed establishes any unusual or improper activity. Townsfolk have repeatedly told me that the baker carried wheat at the bakery and bread at the inn. I also saw the baker stock bread in the market chest and bought two fresh loaves. This appears consistent with baking, stocking the stall, and perhaps supplying the inn, although I have not confirmed the purpose of the inn visit. The baker has not yet answered my questions about town concerns or my tea host.

The builder came to my office seeking a paid repair commission, including specific locations, standards, and an agreed price. I asked for inspection and an itemized estimate before authorizing paid work. My later instruction about a bridge inspection and reporting at one was not heard, so I cannot assume the builder is following it. The secretary told the builder that there was no repair list or approved budget and that my authorization was needed before work began.

The unresolved matter today is my three o'clock tea appointment: the book says a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, without identifying the host or cottage. The secretary said she would try to confirm the address, and I have asked residents and now the baker. I have no evidence that this ambiguity means anything beyond incomplete appointment details. My remaining engagements are lunch at home at noon, town accounts in the office at one, tea at three, office at four-thirty, and home at seven.
